notes.title: The Challenge Update - Now Available!
notes.content:
[p]Hello Squires!  We're landing a huge game update packed with new features that will completely change your experience with The Plucky Squire!  [/p][p][/p][p]This update introduces two new game modes—[b]Challenge Mode and Iron Squire Mode[/b]—along with new enemies, enemy variants, and minigame updates. So if you’ve think it was too easy, The Challenge Update might just change your mind.[/p][p][/p][p]Plus, we’re offering our [b]biggest discount yet[/b] during the Steam Summer Sale![/p][p][/p][previewyoutube="T1K38O_msm8;full"][/previewyoutube][p][/p][p]Here’s the full list of new features and changes that you’ll find in [b]The Challenge Update[/b]:  [/p][p][/p][h3]New Challenge Mode[/h3][p]Challenge Mode is a new game mode designed to test your skills with increased difficulty. This mode includes:[/p][list][*][p] New enemies [/p][/*][*][p] Harder minigames[/p][/*][*][p] Harder bosses [/p][/*][*][p] Some layout changes for levels [/p][/*][*][p] The ability to fast forward through dialogue and [/p][/*][*][p] New Achievements
[/p][/*][/list][h3]Remixed Pages[/h3][p]Pages with combat on have been reworked and side scrolling levels have new layouts.  [/p][p][/p][h3]Humgrump Desk Spawns[/h3][p]In the previous version of the game, we had Humgrump teleport some enemies into the level using his metamagic, but only in the book. We've now added these sequences to the desk too. These spawn in with VFX and a bubble that contains Humgrump's face. Additionally, Jot can get electrified on the desk.  [/p][p][/p][h3]New Metamagic Enemies[/h3][p]Following on from the above, we have the glowing metamagic variants of some of the base enemies. They have their own effects and materials on the desk, and new sprites in the book.[/p][list][*][p] Barfer Bug[/p][/*][*][p] Rat[/p][/*][*][p] Goblin[/p][/*][*][p] Spear Trooper[/p][/*][*][p] Popuff
[/p][/*][/list][h3]Challenge Mode Enemy Variants[/h3][p]We have some upgraded versions of the existing enemies. These are all across both desk and book.[/p][list][*][p] Tough Goblin (just harder)[/p][/*][*][p] Exploding Goblins (run at you and explode)[/p][/*][*][p] Metal Goblins (indestructible)[/p][/*][*][p] Exploding Jumper bugs[/p][/*][*][p] Tough Namastarlings (just harder)[/p][/*][*][p] There's a new tough book-only enemy, the Rock Golem, which appears from Chapter 2.
[/p][/*][/list][h3]More Difficult Minigame Patterns[/h3][p]All of the minigames, apart from the Sneak C09 game, Fish Grabbing and the C04 Fantasy Card Game have new difficulty settings and layouts. Buttergrump also has new patterns. There are little bits of extra functionality in some of these games as a result, such as ghost Archery bugs and new projectiles in Buttergrump.  [/p][p][/p][h3]New Iron Squire Mode[/h3][p]The Plucky Squire with permadeath! This is essentially Challenge Mode but with no continues. As soon as you die in Iron Squire Mode, your save is deleted, and you are sent to a new game over screen. We have one each for desk and the book.  [/p][p][/p][h3]Four New Achievements[/h3][p]There have been five Challenge Mode-specific achievements added.[/p][list][*][p]Complete Challenge Mode: Pops up at the same point that the Adventure/Story Mode one pops up. It also auto-completes the Adventure/Story Mode too.[/p][/*][*][p]Get to Artia in Iron Squire Mode: This triggers at the end of C04 when the camera pans across to show Artia.[/p][/*][*][p]Complete all corrupted (Humgrump) Challenge Mode minigames (without skipping)[/p][list][*][p]Boxing[/p][/*][*][p]Volleyball[/p][/*][*][p]Potion pop[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Complete the Big Brawl at the end of C09 without dying.[/p][p][/p][/*][/list][h3]Dialogue Fast Forward[/h3][p]You can hold the X button or Space Bar to fast forward through all dialogue without repeatedly pressing for each box that pops up.[/p][p][/p][p]The dev team has set up a new form so you can directly send in bug and issue reports to them. If you are encountering problems in the game on the latest versions, please send them over here: [/p][p][/p][p][url="https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSeZcEdKi5xrBuEZbqmRD_MH-eTl4mEps2IwDPDpA9NDuNgqrg/viewform" style="button"]The Plucky Squire Public Bug Submission Form[/url][/p][p][/p][p]Finally, to celebrate, [b]The Plucky Squire is now 35% OFF[/b] in the Steam Summer Sale — our biggest discount yet! Help us spread the word! [/p][p][/p][p][dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/1627570/The_Plucky_Squire/"][/dynamiclink][/p][p]That's all for now, Squires! We hope you enjoy this new adventure![/p][p]
[/p][p][/p][p][/p]

notes.title: Version 1.15.1 adding Streamlined Mode!
notes.content:
[h2]Hello Squires! [/h2]

We’ve added a brand new mode to The Plucky Squire in today’s update. In [i][b]Streamlined Mode[/b][/i], you’ll play through Jot’s adventures at a quicker tempo! We’ve been looking at the feedback about the game, and one of the points that came up was that the pacing was a little too slow for some players. Enter: Streamlined Mode!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42507006/574632c2e69ceffd5593bbb013df893bcd88e299.png[/img]
[h2]Streamlined Mode[/h2]
Streamlined mode is intended for more experienced players who want less guidance and more action. For example! A door unlocks - do you really need the game to stop and the camera to pan over and look at it opening? Maybe not! In Streamlined Mode, it doesn’t! This is one of the many examples of reduced guidance.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42507006/8f55282bf8998c0963eba0c8d43cfa3c45bde224.jpg[/img]
We’ve cut some fat from the dialogue in Streamlined Mode - a line here, a line there... It’s not like we’ve hacked away entire scenes, just trimmed bits for a more…streamlined…experience.

We’ve also added speech bubble portraits to keep track of who’s speaking while you’re speeding through.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42507006/9c8895f728eb7156531977b18affff0bd82ad9c4.png[/img]

Finally, we've included some quality of life improvements and changes. We've increased the number of historical autosaves that are kept and we've added a function to restart the current chapter. If you do get stuck somewhere, both of these should help. Autosaves have been moved to a place in the menu that's easier to find and we've added a way to change the language in-game.

[h2]The Game Awards Nomination and Sale[/h2]

We are deeply honoured to be nominated at The Game Awards for Best Family Game and Best Debut Indie. To thank you and everyone who has supported us, we have put the game on sale for 25% off! Just in time for the Holiday Season! 

The Plucky Squire was inspired by the picture books we loved reading to our children. Our dream was always to create something that families could enjoy together. Whoever makes up your family, we hope The Plucky Squire can bring you and your loved ones some joy!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42507006/a072ba0ab89bc2f9d0f9ec1b14d493e7b789ffac.gif[/img]

[h2]Patch Notes[/h2]
Shiny and New - Streamline Mode:
[list]
[*] Shorter, snappier dialogue that lets you enjoy the story but gets you to the action quicker
[*] Fewer camera events that slow down player action
[*] Added dialogue portraits for major characters
[*] Added an in-game language change option
[*] Added More Save History slots and moved them to "Load Save" in the "Save Files" menu
[/list]
Bug fixes
[list]
[*] Fixed soft lock in credits
[*] Fixed bottom half of Alowynia card being blacked out
[*] Various fixes to collision issues
[/list]

notes.title: The Plucky Squire review
notes.content: Kids today don’t know how good they’ve got it. Sure, the planet’s on fire and they’ll spend most of their future looking after me in a retirement home as I ramble about how good I used to be at Balatro, but have you seen the games they’ve been getting lately? Back in my day, children’s games were dismal 3D platformer movie tie-ins—not magical storybook adventures made with real love and care that ingeniously riff on 2D Zelda, yet also have tons of personality all of their own. notes.title: The Plucky Squire's story starts NOW
notes.content:
[previewyoutube=xREgLxEzZE4;full][/previewyoutube]

[h1]A story 23 years in the making[/h1]

As our studio's first game, we are so grateful that people want to play our game. The first inkling of this game started when James & Bidds met in 2001. Though they went their separate ways, they have wanted to make a game together ever since. 

We are so happy that we can share that game with all of you now. This stunning papercraft launch trailer was made with Paper Engineers, [url=https://www.instagram.com/paperjulia/]Julia Yus[/url] and [url=http://carbonara.es]Yeray Pérez Vallejo[/url].

[i]The Plucky Squire[/i] is now available. We hope it can bring a bit of the joy we felt while making it.

[h1]The story behind the story[/h1]

On a trip to Japan James ended up in an interview for a certain popular game series you may have heard of. 17 years in Japan later, he had many [i]Pokémon[/i] mainline and spinoff games under his belt. 

At the same time Bidds had started his own studio and he was making some very unique stuff. [i]Fluidity[/i] was a liquid-based physics puzzler published by Nintendo while [i]The Swords of Ditto[/i] blended roguelite elements, branching narratives in an rpg adventure. There was even the [i]Stealth[/i] series in between. Which you probably can guess, were stealth games.

After all those escapades and adventures they wanted to return to that original dream. To make their own game together. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42507006/4167a36b78c72821a82e61afeb7b71f92b4a0fe4.png[/img]
James had been honing a visual style and even started an online comic series called [i]Cosmic[/i] which you can see above. From there, they thought of a game that took place in a book. And from there, they wanted to incorporate the 3D elements they had learned along the way. And so the concept of [i]The Plucky Squire[/i] was born. A game in a storybook where you could jump out of the book and into the real 3D world. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42507006/0dadb2a7edc42b052310f94f2dc79c01c0598543.png[/img]

This would be a big technical challenge especially for a very small team. Making fully fleshed out 2D and 3D gameplay would almost be like making 2 entire games. But by putting their heads together, they figured it out. To switch seamlessly between the dimensions the game would render both worlds at the same time, overlaying the 2D gameplay onto 3D objects. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42507006/4af5e191875957a425cd14ba966d380b78ccbe7f.jpg[/img]
From everyone at All Possible Futures, thank you for playing [i]The Plucky Squire[/i]. We hope it's a story to remember.

If you liked reading about development, there is also the Deluxe Edition containing a curated collection of concept art in the form of a digital art book and the official soundtrack by Mike Georgiades. Getting them all together saves you 15% on the whole bundle!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1627570/The_Plucky_Squire/

https://store.steampowered.com/bundle/44990/The_Plucky_Squire_Deluxe_Edition/

notes.title: The Plucky Squire review: a charming storybook adventure, but I wish it let you go full plucko mode
notes.content:
I really wanted to like action adventure The Plucky Squire more than I do now, having given its charming 2D to 3D platforming a proper whirl. Yes, it's lovely to look at. Yes, hopping out of a storybook and making friends with an illustration on a coffee mug is cool. And yes, everyone can have a mildly fun time with its puzzles and fights. But that's the problem: who is everyone? At first I thought, "This game is for young kids and that's fine!", given its relative simplicity. Then I hit some puzzles and thought, "Ain't no kid figuring this out".

Then it hit me. It struggles to balance the fine line between being approachable for tiny tots and layered enough for people who've graduated from "goo goo ga ga" to "oo oo aa aa my back hurts". And that's down to how plucky you're allowed to squire at any given time, because it can be surprisingly limited and, sadly, a bit underwhelming.

notes.title: The Final Plucky Preview
notes.content:
[previewyoutube=fMc0RUJQLqo;full][/previewyoutube]
Here's the final gameplay preview of The Plucky Squire! It only shows a small early part of the game and we still have many surprises in store.

[h3]A Small Preview[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42507006/9804159e287a714e25e76c692ba4ad3f11eb56ae.gif[/img]

Our heroes have chosen to travel through Sonnet Swamps. But when they reach there, they find that they are ill-equipped to help the locals.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42507006/a7d95d20b3f586d03dc03665dfe015902541366a.gif[/img]

Perhaps Jot can use his new found powers to find help in the [i]other[/i] realm. It even looks like some of the book's critters have escaped there as well. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42507006/7bb5477fac6929b13b473f4de17c13add7d417ce.gif[/img]

He'll need to take on these challenges with courage, no matter how many times they may knock him down! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42507006/ff7ee9e741aed8d89e3ba1a2955027747ac07118.gif[/img]

There it is! The elven bow! But how can we convince Alwonyia to help us? Watch the whole preview to find out.

[h3]The Plucky Squire's connection to Shrek?[/h3]
Our whole team is very busy getting everything ready for launch on September 17 but I have a few things to share from our co-founder, James Turner.

Brazilian fans may have noticed that the narrator in Brazilian Portuguese is none other than [b]Mauro Ramos[/b], voice of Shrek, Pumba from The Lion King and Sully from Monsters Inc. [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42507006/c1e3a8dd95a3f19bd48792ad2a5bb909d263bbd9.png[/img]
[h3]Another Game We Love[/h3]
To celebrate the launch of another colorful and playful game today, James has drawn this crossover art with a certain Bot. There are so many amazing games out right now, so we really appreciate that our small team is being put in the same conversations as them!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42507006/c45d1660d9bee725c8df63f534112671a8dbb1b9.png[/img]

notes.title: The Plucky Squire: 11 Localizations and Voice Overs
notes.content:
[previewyoutube=Ky1eS1VafzI;full][/previewyoutube]
Hey everyone,

We're very happy to show you The Plucky Squire in all 11 localizations with full audio and their voice over actors!

It was a big challenge to bring the game to each new language. In our game, words aren't just on the UI, they're gameplay objects that effect the world. We've done our best to ensure that each word puzzle makes sense in all 11 localizations, along with all the bonus possibilities when you throw unintended word combinations together.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42507006/ec8699b7fd564f70768bd07d3120b178e5d422a0.gif[/img]

We also wanted to thank our brilliant voice actors and linguists who have helped bring our story to life in each of these versions. 

Voice actors:

[list]

notes.title: Adorable and reality-bending action-puzzle game The Plucky Squire lets you make friends with a Magic: The Gathering card
notes.content: I think if I discovered my entire life was just a story in a children's picture book, I'd probably have quite a serious breakdown. Jot, the eponymous hero of The Plucky Squire, seems unfazed by it all, however—even as he leaps from the pages of his book and discovers an entirely new 3D reality beyond his own... Read more.

notes.title: The Plucky Squire, one of 2024's coolest looking indies, is launching day one on PlayStation Plus
notes.content:
The Plucky Squire - one of the coolest looking indie games set to release this year - has finally got itself a release date. It's going to launch on September 17, but PlayStation Plus subscribers will be happy to learn that they'll be able to download it day-one.

This was announced via the official PlayStation Twitter account, and was paired with a lovely little gameplay video showcasing the game. The game will be added to the PlayStation Plus games catalogue, so even if you decide to sign up a little later in the year The Plucky Squire should be there waiting for you.

The Plucky Squire, for those who don't know, is looking especially rad in an already-stacked year of slick releases. It blends 2D and 3D gameplay together in an uber colourful drawing book style aesthetic that's damn pleasing to the eye. The developer, All Possible Futures, is releasing it as its first game with Devolver Digital as a publisher, and if Devolver's name isn't a stamp of approval at this point for ambitious, amazing indies then I don't know what to tell you.

Read more

notes.title: We are launching The Plucky Squire on September 17!
notes.content:
[previewyoutube=4DpvZWrts_M;full][/previewyoutube]

[h1]The tale of The Plucky Squire will begin September 17, 2024![/h1]

[h2]A message from us[/h2]
From the heights of Honey Peak to the shores of Boogie Beach, we can’t wait to share our debut game and the world of The Plucky Squire with you. 

It's been a long road to get here and it's hard to believe that we'll finally be launching in one month. But in spite of the hours, months and years that have gone into it, it has truly been a joy making this game. 

Our aim was to capture the childhood wonder of playing games. Games on screens, on tabletops and in the world of make-believe. We initially planned for the game to be about 3-5 hours long but as development progressed, it felt right to try and fit in more and more of those wondrous moments. 

So we've doubled that initial content and we expect you to take about 8-10 hours in a first playthrough! 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42507006/25c693a128955e822dfad6f0d3212e90428f3bf0.gif[/img]

[h2]Early Prototypes[/h2]
As we approach launch, we've been looking back at some of the very early tech tests. Back then, we weren't even sure whether the scope of what we envisioned was possible with our resources. Things have come a long way since then!

Let us know if you'd like to see more about the game and our development! You can [b]follow[/b] us here on Steam to see everything we share. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42507006/d57fdfc0a6f264667401e087f465f6b4215f54da.gif[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42507006/18448c9c153cd8961dc5027a298b625cbfd8a336.gif[/img]

[h2]Your tale begins on September 17[/h2]
Finally, we'd like to thank you for following our game's progress. Individually, we've worked on a lot of games, but this is the first one we're making as All Possible Futures. You've shown faith in us and we hope we can repay it with a special experience on September 17. 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42507006/150414f549ebeed5c9c231427e6c752756f6aa11.gif[/img]

Are you curious to see what our friend Jot and his friends are up to on their adventures in The Plucky Squire? You can find out in the latest gameplay video streamed as part of the IGN Fan Fest 2024.

The new video follows Jot as he solves a series of puzzles in a mine, demonstrating some of the different mechanics you'll get to play with, including jumping in and out of the book to bypass obstacles, and tilting the book to move things around. The video also introduces some of his friends you'll encounter on your journey.

Stay tuned for more on The Plucky Squire as we get closer to launch later this year.

notes.title: The Plucky Squire revealed, an endearing storybook adventure that blends 2D and 3D gameplay
notes.content:
Former Pokemon art director, James Turner, renowned for his work on Pokemon Sword and Shield, unveiled just yesterday that he had moved on from GAME FREAK. As a result, Turner announced that he had started his own studio, All Possible Futures, with The Swords of Ditto developer, @onebitbeyond.

In the announcement, Turner teased that their first game would be revealed very soon, and he wasn't lying. As the Devolver Digital Showcase unfolded, we got our first peek at The Plucky Squire, which will be coming to PC, PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X/S, and Nintendo Switch in 2023.

Admittedly, the childlike look of The Plucky Squire lost my interest at first, which is amusing considering my favourite game series is about a pink puff ball called Kirby. Yet, as soon as the trailer revealed a blend between 2D and 3D worlds, as one character popped out from the pages, I considered myself obsessed, and thought everyone else should too.

Read more

notes.title: The Plucky Squire managed to melt my E3-hardened heart
notes.content: I gotta be honest: when the trailer for the Plucky Squire opened with a view of a Toy Story-esque child's room, softly lit in the afternoon light, I was prepared to check out. "This is probably not for me," I thought. But as the Plucky Squire storybook opened up to reveal top-down, Zelda-style gameplay in a gorgeous, 2D animation style, I changed my tune quick... Read more.
